doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Current playing and writing; 'Blue Flame' on clarinet
summary: He is retired as emeritus, busy as a player in Florida, and writes weekly for his quartet. He plays Woody Herman's theme 'Blue Flame' and credits his vibrato to Sidney Bechet.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And you’ve been honored as a Professor Emeritus?

Well that’s kind of sort of when you’re retiring they put you on this shelf you know. But it’s good, for I just wrote a reference letter for a friend of mine that wants to get a teaching job down here, and I used it then.
It gives it some weight. What is your playing schedule like nowadays?

Well I’ve been busier the last two months as a player than I have been in years really. And I’m having a ball with it, I really love it. And I’m not doing a lot of writing but I still write some. Unless I have commissions to write I wouldn’t get into it seriously, but I always write, every week I usually write something. I have a quartet that I’ve been working on down here and I write for it mainly, and I’m working on doing some standard tunes which these people down here will relate to but I’m having kind of a variable time signature thing where the rhythm section will be playing in twelve-eight, we’re playing in four. Sometimes I’m shifting around and things like that. So it’s an interesting thing. It keeps me out of trouble.
Well you have your clarinet there, and I would love to have you play something of your choice.
